data.title: The record funding years
data.content:
# The record funding years

The shortest era on this page, and the one that shaped what most people still
expect a hiring process to look like. Funding raised in a single year roughly
doubled the previous record, and headcount plans were written against that
capital rather than against revenue.

Two things followed that are worth stating plainly, because they are the
baseline everything after 2022 is measured against. Roles were opened before the
work that would fill them existed. And the constraint an employer optimised for
was time-to-fill — which is the only condition under which a process gets
shorter rather than longer.
data.summary: Two years in which the policy floor returned and venture funding roughly doubled its previous record. Headcount plans were set against committed capital rather than against bookings, and the terms of entry were set on the candidate's side.
data.capital: The policy rate returned to 0.00–0.25% on 16 March 2020 and stayed there for two years. US venture-backed companies raised $329.6 billion in 2021 against a previous record of $166.6 billion in 2020, and global venture investment reached $671 billion. The listing window stayed open to companies without earnings: of 121 US technology listings in 2021, 21% were profitable on trailing twelve-month earnings.
data.hiring: With several years of funding raised at once, headcount was planned against committed capital rather than against bookings, and roles were opened before the work that would fill them was specified. Time-to-fill became the operative constraint, so loops were shortened, offers raised and candidate pools widened across locations. Recruiting functions were themselves staffed to the expanded plan.
data.entry: Employers competed for candidates, so entry terms were set on the candidate's side: compressed interview loops, offers made on shorter evidence, and pay set by competing bids. Entry-level and career-change intake ran at volume, because the alternative was leaving funded seats empty. Holding a current job was not a precondition, and changing employer was the ordinary way to raise pay.
data.ended_by: Two dated changes. The target range left the floor on 17 March 2022, and for tax years beginning after 31 December 2021 any amount paid in connection with developing software had to be capitalised and amortised over five years — so a developer's salary stopped reducing taxable income in the year it was paid.
